messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: rstan: storing paths of more than 100 bytes is not portable:
parts:
I just build rstan with R 3.0.1 and got (from make build in the
rstan/rstan directory)

* checking for empty or unneeded directories
Removed empty directory ï¿½rstan/inst/include/stansrc/models/bugs_examples/vol2/biopsiesï¿½
Removed empty directory ï¿½rstan/inst/include/stansrc/models/bugs_examples/vol3/jamaï¿½
* adding MD5 file
* building ï¿½rstan_2.0.1.tar.gzï¿½
Warning in utils::tar(filepath, pkgname, compression = "gzip", compression_level = 9L, :
storing paths of more than 100 bytes is not portable:
ï¿½rstan/inst/include/stanlib/boost_1.54.0/boost/accumulators/framework/accumulators/droppable_accumulator.hppï¿½
Warning in utils::tar(filepath, pkgname, compression = "gzip", compression_level = 9L, :
storing paths of more than 100 bytes is not portable:

and many more warnings about the path length.

I'm guessing this is a new check added by R, since I didn't see it with
R 2.15.1.

I'm assuming since I have gnu utilities (Debian) this is not actually an
issue for me; I just thought I'd report it here.

Ross Boylan
